subject: Refining support commitments and maintenance windows — Helios Order Form
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helios order form — timing on SLA redlines and maintenance windows

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Looping you in on Helios' redline request for the MSA/order form. Attached is the current Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_v3.docx) they returned with a few specific asks around uptime targets, scheduled maintenance windows, and the service credit formula. High-level asks from their tech and ops team:

- Tighten availability on the critical inference endpoint to 99.97% (they want stronger guarantees for production reads).
- Limit scheduled maintenance so it never overlaps their month-end ETL (they called out last business-day windows).
- Swap our flat credit slab for a stepped credit tied to outage duration and affected region.

Can you advise on what we can flex on without blowing the pricing model? I'd like to put together a single-proposal response to keep legal review short.

Attachments: Redwood_OrderForm_v3.docx (order form with markup)

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal proposal (ops + sales) to present a narrow counter (availability + blackout windows + credit cap).
2) Legal to scope redline on MSA language for maintenance carveouts and evidence.
3) Draft appendix with monitoring / audit log access and SOC2 summary.

I'm available for a quick sync at 11:00 if helpful.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Pedro Alvarez <pedro@helios.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ana Torres <ana.torres@helios.com>, ops-legal@helios.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios order form — timing on SLA redlines and maintenance windows

Mateo —

Thanks for the heads up and the doc. We reviewed internally and attached a short redline called Helios_Redlines_SLA.docx with the team's asks. Summary below:

1) Availability: For the production inference endpoint (api.prod.infer), we need 99.97% monthly availability. Non-critical endpoints can stay at 99.90%.

2) Response times & incident ladder: P1 (complete service disruption affecting >50% of traffic) — 4 hour response / mitigation SLA and 12 hour time-to-resolution target for initial fix; P2 — 8 hour response. We understand the difference between response and resolution; these are operational commitments for detection + acknowledgement + mitigation steps.

3) Maintenance windows: Scheduled maintenance must be notified 30 days in advance. We need an explicit blackout for the last business day of each month (00:00-08:00 UTC) and no more than 4 hours of scheduled downtime in that blackout window per quarter.

4) Credits: We prefer a stepped credit with an initial threshold at 99.97% (5% credit), 99.90%-99.97% (3% credit), below 99.90% escalates (10% credit). Cap credits at 50% monthly invoice.

5) Evidence: access to monthly availability reports, incident timelines, and a scoped audit pack (SOC2 summary + uptime graphs).

We know some asks are aggressive — happy to discuss compromises. Ana (cc'd) will handle the legal redline if we can agree on the operational points.

Regards,
Pedro Alvarez
Head of Platform Ops | Helios Systems
pedro@helios.com

Attachment: Helios_Redlines_SLA.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios order form — timing on SLA redlines and maintenance windows

Team —

Thanks Pedro for the clear asks. Internal thinking: Helios' availability target for the critical endpoint is reasonable for their use case but will change our capacity and pricing posture if we guarantee 99.97% for single-region deployments. Thoughts and a suggested compromise:

- Offer multi-region active-active for api.prod.infer at 99.97% (this is a paid option) or single-region at 99.95% with a defined failover playbook. That lets us keep pricing rational while meeting their operational need.

- Maintenance windows: agree to the month-end blackout (last business day 00:00-08:00 UTC) but restrict total scheduled maintenance across all regions to <= 8 hours per month and ensure we provide a planned maintenance calendar 30 days out. For emergencies we keep the right to apply hotfix windows but with advanced notice where possible.

- Credits: propose a stepped credit but with a lower cap (35% monthly invoice) and an initial threshold of 99.95% (2% credit), 99.90%-99.95% (5% credit), <99.90% (12% credit). Explain the multi-region priced option separately.

Action items:
1) Legal (Laura) — please prep redline text for the maintenance blackout, evidence rights (monthly report + 30 day incident archive), and the credit cap language.
2) Mateo — please send a one-pager to Pedro outlining the multi-region pricing delta so they can decide quickly.
3) I'll draft the SLA appendix table with the negotiated thresholds and credit math (attach as XLSX).

I attached a working table (SLA_Table_vProposed.xlsx) with the credit math.

-Marissa
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: SLA_Table_vProposed.xlsx

From: Ana Torres <ana.torres@helios.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
Cc: Pedro Alvarez <pedro@helios.com>, ops-legal@helios.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios order form — timing on SLA redlines and maintenance windows

Marissa / Mateo —

Thanks for the proposed compromise. A few legal points from our side before we hand this back to procurement:

- Evidence and audit: Helios requires an explicit statement about the retention period for incident logs (minimum 90 days), and a commitment that Redwood will provide, on request, a redacted incident timeline within 5 business days for any P1/P2 incident.

- Credit mechanics: we need clarity that credits are calculated as a percentage of the monthly service fees (not including pass-through infrastructure charges) and that credits will be applied to the next invoice.

- Indemnities & uptime measurement: please define the exact monitoring endpoints used to measure availability (we prefer api.prod.infer healthcheck on port 443 and the /healthz endpoint). If there are synthetic checks, disclose their location and frequency.

We can prepare a concise legal redline once you incorporate the log retention and measurement definitions.

Best,
Ana Torres
Senior Counsel | Helios Systems
ana.torres@helios.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Pedro Alvarez <pedro@helios.com>, Ana Torres <ana.torres@helios.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios order form — timing on SLA redlines and maintenance windows

Pedro / Ana —

Appreciate the quick responses and the pragmatic feedback. Summary of the team-aligned proposal (so legal has a clear base to redline):

- Availability: Offer 99.97% for api.prod.infer as an opt-in, multi-region active-active add-on (we will price this as a plus for resiliency). For single-region baseline we will commit to 99.95%.

- Maintenance blackout: Last business day 00:00-08:00 UTC will be a no-scheduled-maintenance window. Total scheduled maintenance across regions will be <= 8 hours/month (we'll track on a shared calendar). Planned maintenance will be notified 30 days in advance. Emergency hotfixes permitted with post-event commentary.

- Credits: Stepped credit table (see attached SLA_Appendix_proposal.pdf) with a 35% monthly cap (credits applied to next invoice). Credits calculated against Redwood service fees only.

- Evidence & monitoring: We'll publish the measurement definition for api.prod.infer (TLS healthcheck on port 443, /healthz synthetic probe from three independent regions at 5-min cadence). Incident logs retained for 90 days; for P1/P2 incidents we'll provide a redacted timeline within 5 business days.

Attachments: SLA_Appendix_proposal.pdf (proposed appendix with metric definitions and credit math)
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/hl-4821-msav3 (we will attach the appendix to the MSA for signature after legal alignment)

Next steps:
- Ana / Helios legal: please produce the redline against the MSA and SLA appendix; Laura (cc) will coordinate Redwood legal comments.
- Pedro / Helios ops: if you can confirm the multi-region pricing acceptance, Mateo will finalize the commercial appendix by EOD Friday.
- Marissa: will circulate the final SLA table and credit math to the Helios procurement owner.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.ai

Attachment: SLA_Appendix_proposal.pdf
